In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the oxygen fluctuations are the major factor controlling the foraminifera assemblage composition, while the sea-level fluctuations are the major factors controlling the foraminiferan assemblage distribution.
, in the studied succession, the oxygen fluctuations have been a major controlling factor in the benthic microhabitat distribution, but they have not controlled the overall assemblage composition.
the oxygen fluctuations recorded during the Pleistocene are not only related to sea-level changes but also to the oxygen penetration within sediment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the Pleistocene the benthic faunal changes are mainly related to the cyclic changes in oxygenation, whereas the sea-level oscillations are of secondary importance.
the oxygenation changes recorded in the Montalbano section are related to the sea level changes and that the benthic microhabitat distribution is controlled by the bottom-water oxygenation.
, at the base of the section (from 0.9 to 0.7 Ma), the assemblages were characterized by a high abundance of infaunal species, and by a low diversity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
foraminiferal data can be used as a proxy of the bottom-water oxygen fluctuations, and that foraminifera are a useful tool in palaeoenvironmental studies.

the microhabitat distribution of foraminiferal species is an important factor in the interpretation of the palaeoenvironmental conditions and that it should be considered in the reconstruction of the oxygen fluctuations in the past.
the benthic oxygen fluctuations recorded in this composite section are in phase with the global oxygen fluctuations recorded in deep-sea sediments.
